title: Fitted SST radiation gains improve six-year holdout predictions in four of seven model pairs for 1979-2014
abstract: We test whether large fitted SST radiation gains predict time blocks left out of seven AMIPII-minus-HadISST2 model comparisons. Full-record annual gains reproduce the earlier median of 1.88. With six-year holdouts and one-year training gaps, fitting the five-model Green's-function gain reduces mean squared prediction error in four pairs and increases it in three. The same split holds when endpoint blocks are omitted. Starting in 1985 reduces the median prediction benefit from 10.6% to 1.0%. MPI improves across all tested trend choices and block lengths, while other results depend on those choices. Large full-record gains alone do not establish a common multiplier for SST artifact effects. These are retrospective prediction tests of signed aggregate series, not new model runs or a test of which SST record is correct. Configuration differences, short records and correlated errors limit causal and statistical claims.

display.caption: Annual fitted gains by period, and six-year holdout prediction error. Positive error reduction means a fitted gain improves on gain one. Cubic time terms and a sea-ice term are fit on training years only.

citations.reason: We reuse signed aggregate series and test the transfer of the fitted radiation gain to omitted time blocks. We qualify its broad artifact lower-bound inference, not its measured SST steps.
